market_commentary:
North American equity indices advanced and crude extended its run in the week ending May 14 — the S&P/TSX Composite rose +1.2% to 34,26822, while the S&P 500 gained +2.2% to 7,501 and the Nasdaq added +3.2% to 26,635. WTI crude settled at US$100.16/bbl, up +5.0% on the week and +60.1% year over year, with Brent at US$108.59/bbl (+7.2%) following the Strait of Hormuz supply disruption1920. The Canadian dollar eased -0.6% to 0.7276 CAD/USD. The database tracks 7,480 active and proposed projects valued at $1,472.2 billion.

The project pipeline's exposure split between rate-sensitive financing and commodity pricing — the database contains 211 residential projects ($32.2 billion) and 1,663 infrastructure projects ($210.3 billion) that carry rate-sensitive financing against the Bank of Canada's 2.25% policy rate and a 6.09% prime rate1. The 10-year Government of Canada yield stood at 3.56%, up from 3.06% a year earlier, with the 2-10 spread at 60 basis points. The database also tracks 59 oil and gas projects ($97.6 billion) and 390 mining projects ($227.1 billion); if WTI holds above US$100, these energy projects price against a level +60.1% above the year-ago benchmark20.
